content:
incident-bot: ALERT: High timeout/error rate detected for /v1/generate · error_rate(5xx+timeout) > 4.8% over last 5m · p95=1.42s p99=8.23s · grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/serve/prod-overview
Erin: oncall here, paging in. seeing the same on dashboard. starting triage. @SRE-Lead are you around?
SRE-Lead: here, looking. any recent deploys or config changes?
deploy-bot: deploy COMPLETE: rollout id=rl-2026-03-15-0923 commit=abcd123 to cluster=prod at 5201234500
Miguel: that rollout touched serving runtime + kvcache tuning for v2-model. I saw a small bump during canary but it was within limits then.
Alice: checking logs for 5xx pattern now. quick grep shows a lot of upstream timeouts -> `gateway: upstream timeout` and `http: read/write timeout` spikes. sample:
```

162.3.44.12 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:25:11 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 504 0 "-" "sdk/1.2.3" rt=8.212s
service=broker handler=call model=v2 tags="kvcache=on" error="upstream timeout"
```

Erin: metric dive: error_rate spiked at 09:23:40 right after rollout completion. p50 stable, p95 jumped to 1.4s and p99 exploded. tail shows connection pool saturation + long GC in worker pods.
Miguel: I see `connection refused` and `connection reset` to model backends around same timestamps. probably client-side conn pool exhaustion due to new kernel flags? also kvcache warmups causing sudden mem pressure.
SRE-Lead: This is impacting customer-facing latency SLOs. recommend immediate rollback to previous revision and open a mitigation path (route-shift + circuit-breaker). Erin, can you trigger rollback?
Erin: initiating rollback now. running: `infra deploy rollback --to rl-2026-03-14-2310`
deploy-bot: ROLLBACK STARTED: rollback id=rb-5201234567 parent=rl-2026-03-15-0923
Erin: disabling kvcache feature-flag for v2 while rolling back: `ffctl set kvcache_v2 false --env prod`
Alice: patching HTTP gateway circuit-breaker to 20% for /v1/generate to shed some load: `gatewayctl set-cb /v1/generate 20%`
SRE-Lead: good. also enabling fallback model route: route /v1/generate -> v1-stable if v2 responds > 2s.
Miguel: pushing a temporary increase to model backend connpool from 100 -> 300 for node-pool B to tolerate warmup.
Support-Bot: PagerDuty P0 acknowledged. Notifying ~ops-team and ~support for possible customer notices.
Eva: product here. any idea on customer impact? numbers?
Erin: approx 12% of requests to /v1/generate failing or timing out during the 09:23-09:32 window. Top affected tenants: AcmeCorp, BrightShop, Queryly (enterprise). support can start outreach for top 3.
Support-Bot: creating support tickets for the three affected customers and putting them on high-priority queue. ticket refs: SUP-1160, SUP-1161, SUP-1162
Miguel: rollback progress: ~70% of pods reverted, new pods terminating cleanly. seeing gradual drop in connection resets.
deploy-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE: rollback id=rb-5201234567 -> target=rl-2026-03-14-2310 at 5201234595
Erin: monitoring after rollback — error rate trending down. p95 back to ~180ms, p99 back to 420ms. still watching for residual tail.
Alice: logs post-rollback look much cleaner. sample success request:
```
162.3.44.12 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:31:12 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 5123 "-" "sdk/1.2.3" rt=0.182s
```

SRE-Lead: great. let's keep route-shift/cb for another 30m then remove. also collect heap/GC traces from the v2 experiment pods for postmortem. owner: Miguel.
Miguel: will grab `jstack`/heapdump and upload to artifacts. tagging with the rollout id.
Eva: drafting status update for affected customers. will coordinate with support on timing.
Support-Bot: support tickets updated with incident summary + rollback note. cc: CSMs.
Erin: handing off to daytime oncall (Alice) at 09:50 UTC for continued monitoring.
Alice: on it. I'll keep the circuit-breaker and route fallback until 10:15 and then remove if stable.
SRE-Lead: postmortem owner assigned: Miguel. expected initial draft within 48h. include: rollout plan review, kvcache memuse, connpool sizing, graceful warmup.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) · root cause suspected: v2 kvcache/serving runtime change causing connection pool exhaustion and backend timeouts during warmup · follow-up: postmortem assigned
Erin: thanks everyone. great quick work — saved the SLOs. :thumbsup:
Support-Bot: customers notified. closing support loop once we confirm each customer no longer seeing errors.
Alice: final note — add a canary safety gate for memory and conn-reset metrics to the rollout checklist.
SRE-Lead: agreed. will add gating to CI and update runbook. handing off to operations for long-term fixes.
